html:
The Taungurung, also spelled Daungwurrung, are an Aboriginal Australian people of central Victoria and one of the five nations of the Kulin alliance. Their country lies north of the Great Dividing Range, in the valleys of the Goulburn, Broken and upper Campaspe rivers, and they were made up of nine clans.

They shared language and law with their Kulin neighbours, the Wurundjeri to the south, the Boonwurrung on Port Phillip Bay and the Dja Dja Wurrung to the west. Marriage and ceremony tied the clans of these nations together.

Sheep runs spread over their country from the late 1830s. In 1859 Taungurung and Wurundjeri leaders asked for land on the Acheron River to farm. They were moved on, and in 1863 the survivors settled at Coranderrk near Healesville, a station they ran with great success until the government closed it down. Taungurung people today hold a settlement agreement with the state of Victoria over their country.
